title: The QCLI-267 --post provenance gate checks npm's unsigned gitHead, not the signed SLSA attestation quest packages also carry
description: Raised by lore-cli while adapting QCLI-267's runbook fix for their own repository (LCLI-481). scripts/qualification/release-provenance.mjs --post (QCLI-267) reads only `npm view <name>@<version> gitHead`, plain unsigned packument metadata. This session separately confirmed @opum-ai/quest DOES carry a slsa.dev/provenance/v1 attestation on every version from 0.3.0 through 0.6.0 (npm view @opum-ai/quest@<v> dist.attestations --json). The attestation embeds its own commit reference (predicate.buildDefinition.resolvedDependencies[0].digest.gitCommit) and build run id (predicate.runDetails.metadata.invocationId), signed rather than plain packument metadata. The --post gate currently checks only the weaker surface. In the case that produced QCLI-267 the two would have agreed (both come from the same publish), so this is not known to have produced a false pass yet -- but nothing here confirms the gate would catch a future case where they diverge, or verifies the attestation's own embedded commit at all. lore-cli is building LCLI-481 (their equivalent) against the attestation surface for exactly this reason, since @opum-ai/lore* packages publish no gitHead field at all and their dangling reference lives ONLY in the attestation.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Confirmed whether quest packages publishing attestations means gitHead and the attestations embedded gitCommit could ever diverge for a legitimate publish, or whether they are guaranteed identical by how npm publish -- provenance works

A decision recorded on whether --post should also verify the attestations embedded gitCommit/invocationId, verify gitHead only (current behavior, with the reason this is sufficient), or verify the attestation instead of gitHead
If the gate changes, release-provenance.mjs --post is updated and the change is exercised against a real published version the way QCLI-267s negative tests were
